items.title: Nikita Kucherov sets Lightning team scoring record
items.summary: Nikita Kucherov passed Steven Stamkos for the most points in Tampa Bay Lightning franchise history.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: David Kirouac-USA TODAY Sports There’s a new all-time points leader in Tampa Bay Lightning franchise history. Forward Nikita Kucherov assisted on Brayden Point’s power-play goal in the first period against the Utah Mammoth , which gave the Lightning a 3-1 lead and Kucherov the 1,138th point of his career, one more than Steven Stamkos’ franchise record and handing the title to the Tampa Bay winger. Kucherov tied the franchise record Wednesday after he scored against the Vegas Golden Knights . In 13 NHL regular seasons, Kucherov has 405 goals and 733 assists for 1,138 points in 890 career games. During that span, he’s recorded six 100-point campaigns, four 40-goal seasons and five 80-assist campaigns. In 2023-24, Kucherov became the fifth player in NHL history to record 100 assists in a single season . That season, he recorded career highs across the board with 44 goals and 100 assists for 144 points. He’s led the league in both assists and points three times during his career (2018-19, 2023-24 and 2024-25). Kucherov also recorded his 1,000th career point in 2025-26. Kucherov also scored 54 goals and recorded 123 assists for 177 points in 159 career playoff games. He was a major factor in the Lightning’s back-to-back Stanley Cup championships in 2020 and 2021, and helped the club reach the Stanley Cup Final two more times in 2015 and 2022. The native of Maykop, Russia, has earned several individual awards through his career. He won the Art Ross Trophy three times, the Hart Trophy twice and the Ted Lindsay Award twice. Going into Saturday night, the Lightning were 7-3-0 through their first 10 games of 2026-27. Kucherov and Brandon Hagel were tied for the team lead in points with 13.

The game was Ovechkin’s 10th of the 2026-27 season, triggering the $4.75 million performance bonus in the one-year contract he signed with the Capitals to return for his 22nd and final NHL season . With the 10-game mark hit, Ovechkin will earn $9 million this year: $1 million in base salary and $3.25 million in signing bonus making up the remainder. Despite earning the bonus, Ovechkin’s cap hit this season will remain $4.25 million. However, depending on how much cap space the Capitals have at season’s end, a portion of Ovechkin’s bonus, or all of it, will carry over and count against next year’s salary cap even though the legendary winger will no longer be on the club’s roster. According to PuckPedia , the Capitals currently have $2.31 million in cap space, mainly because Rasmus Sandin is on long-term injured reserve. They project the Caps will be $1.36 million over the cap at season’s end, meaning the full Ovechkin bonus will likely extend into next year’s available funds. Through 10 games this season, the 41-year-old Ovechkin has notched just four points (1g, 3a), the weakest start to a campaign in his career. He is also playing a much smaller role than in previous years, skating just 14:12 per game coming into Saturday’s contest and no longer remaining on the ice for the full two minutes of Washington’s power plays. Ovechkin officially announced on October 5 that this season will be his last in the NHL. items.title: Surging Leafs scorch Oilers for fourth win in a row
items.summary: William Nylander had two goals, including the 300th of his career, as the Toronto Maple Leafs scorched the Edmonton Oilers 7-2 on Saturday.
items.body: EDMONTON — William Nylander had two goals, including the 300th of his career, as the Toronto Maple Leafs scorched the Edmonton Oilers 7-2 on Saturday. Jack Roslovic, Auston Matthews, Troy Stecher, Zack MacEwen and Vinni Lettieri also scored for the Maple Leafs (7-4-2) who have won four straight. Anthony Stolarz made 30 stops to earn the win in the Toronto net. Leon Draisaitl scored twice for the Oilers (8-2-1) who had a three-game winning streak halted. With his league-leading 12th goal, Draisaitl recorded his third consecutive two-goal game and extended his goal-scoring streak to six games, during which he has nine goals. Maple Leafs: Matthews and Kirill Marchenko both extended their season-opening road point streak to five games. Matthews now needs just one point to reach 800 in his career, which will make him the fastest player in franchise history to reach the milestone, in addition to the NHL’s third quickest American skater to hit the mark. Oilers: Connor McDavid had two assists to extend his season-starting points streak to 11 games — giving him an incredible 33 points in 11 games. McDavid entered the contest scoring at a staggering 3.10 points-per-game rate. Just 54 seconds after going up 2-0, Kirill Marchenko made a nice pass to hit Stecher in flight in the slot and he scored his second goal of the season in as many games. No team has had more success in Rogers Place in Edmonton than the Maple Leafs. Since the Oilers moved into their new arena, Toronto has gone 12-2-1. The Maple Leafs have been impressive this season on the PK. They had killed 40 of 41 opposition power plays and 30 in a row until Edmonton got one late in Saturday's game.

items.title: Hurricanes tried trading for forward to flip to Jets for Hellebuyck
items.body: The reigning Stanley Cup champions were trying to make a blockbuster. Sportnet's Elliotte Friedman reported on Saturday Headlines that the Carolina Hurricanes made a big effort to trade for Connor Hellebuyck , and they were willing to get creative to make a deal happen. "They tried to reach out to other teams to figure out forwards that the Jets might have interest in, and they were going to trade for those players, and flip that player to the Jets to get Hellebuyck," Friedman said. A deal never came to fruition, as Hellebuyck was sent to the New Jersey Devils on Friday for prospect Alexander Command, goalie Nico Daws, forwards Dawson Mercer and Nick Bjugstad and a pair of draft picks. Friedman added that the Jets wanted "immediate forward help" in the return for their long-time goalie, and the Hurricanes weren't willing to include players like Seth Jarvis, Logan Stankoven or Jackson Blake in a trade. So the Hurricanes tried other avenues, but were beaten to the punch by the Devils. Losing out on the Hellebuyck sweepstakes means Carolina will continue to roll with their goalie tandem of Brandon Bussi and Pyotr Kochetkov. Each netminder has started six games this season, with Kochetkov outperforming Bussi in both goals-against average and save percentage. The Hurricanes entered Saturday's game against the St. Louis Blues first in the Metropolitan Division with an 8-2-2 record.

items.body: Register Login Dallas Stars Injury Updates By Brennan McClain | at October 24, 2026 8:01 pm The Dallas Stars made an expected change to their injured reserve earlier today. Dallas announced that they placed forward Oskar Back on the long-term injured reserve and defenseman Esa Lindell on the normal injured reserve. Given that they’ve opened two roster spots, Dallas will likely recall a player from AHL Texas. Independent correspondent Robert Tiffin reports that the Stars will be without Sam Steel tomorrow after he received a treatment injection today. Forwards Radek Faksa and David Perron are also question marks, so it would make sense for the Stars to recall a forward. Back has been out of Dallas’ lineup since October 14th. The 26-year-old forward broke his finger in the Stars’ shootout win over the Colorado Avalanche, and isn’t expected back until mid-to-late November. With all due respect to Back, he should be fairly replaceable in Dallas’ bottom six. He scored nine goals and 28 points in 145 games throughout his first two years with the Stars, and has registered one assist in seven games this year. Meanwhile, Lindell will be much trickier to replace. Arguably the Stars’ top defensive defenseman, Lindell has been recovering from a lower-body injury since October 17th. Although he is eligible to return tomorrow, today’s roster move suggests he is not quite ready yet. However, Dallas will have the option to activate him when he is healthy in the coming days. On the year, Lindell has done what he does best. He’s gone scoreless in eight games, but has 18 blocked shots and has managed an exceptional 98.1% on-ice SV% at even strength.

items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: James Guillory-Imagn Images The Tampa Bay Lightning announced that defenseman Victor Hedman will not play in Saturday’s game against the Utah Mammoth and will be day-to-day with a lower-body injury. Hedman left Friday’s game against the Colorado Avalanche after he took one shift in the second period and did not return. The team did not provide a reason for his absence during the game, and head coach Jon Cooper didn’t bring Hedman up during his post-game media availability. Hedman skated for only one shift in the second period and did not come out for the final frame. He finished the night with 5:56 of ice time and the Lightning lost 6-3. Through his first nine games, Hedman has two goals and two assists for four points. Now in his 18th NHL season, the 35-year-old native of Ornskoldsvik, Sweden, has 174 goals and 641 assists for 815 points in 1,174 career NHL games. Hedman also has 23 goals and 97 assists for 120 points in 170 career playoff games. He led the Lightning to back-to-back Stanley Cup championships in 2020 and 2021, and helped the team reach the Stanley Cup Final in 2015 and 2022. He won the Norris Trophy for the league’s top defender in 2018 and the Conn Smythe Trophy for Playoff MVP in 2020. The Lightning are 7-3-0 through their first 10 games of 2026-27. Forwards Brandon Hagel and Nikita Kucherov are tied with a team-leading 13 points , while Andrei Vasilevskiy is 5-2-0 with an .884 save percentage .

items.body: New Jersey players excited about ‘huge splash’ of three-time Vezina winner’s acquisition NEWARK, N.J. -- Jack Hughes understands why the trade has created so much noise. The New Jersey Devils center believes the acquisition of Connor Hellebuyck from the Winnipeg Jets deserves every bit of it. "There should be a lot of noise about it," Hughes said. "It's a huge splash for our team, our market. It shows us that our ownership and our management is putting the pieces together to give us a great opportunity to win every night." The challenge for New Jersey was turning down the volume long enough to play. One day after the trade, they completed an unbeaten homestand (3-0-0) with a 3-1 win against the Los Angeles Kings on Saturday. That has provided positive momentum before beginning a three-game road trip at the Dallas Stars on Tuesday and welcoming one of the NHL's premier goalies into the group. Hughes already knows what Hellebuyck can bring. The two played together for the United States at the 2026 Winter Olympics and won the gold medal. items.body: Register Login Wild Recall Mason Shaw By Brennan McClain | at October 24, 2026 7:00 pm The Minnesota Wild have added familiar depth at forward after losing defenseman Daemon Hunt on waivers. According to a team announcement , the Wild recalled forward Mason Shaw from the AHL’s Iowa Wild. Shaw, 27, is in his second stint with the Wild. Minnesota selected him with the 97th overall pick (fourth round) in the 2017 NHL Draft. He played in the WHL for the Medicine Hat Tigers and made his professional debut in the 2017-18 season. Throughout his first stint with the Wild, Shaw primarily played in the AHL. Still, in the 2022-23 season, Shaw skated in 59 NHL contests, scoring seven goals and 17 points with a -1 rating. Unfortunately, injuries have followed Shaw throughout his career. Before debuting in the NHL, Shaw tore his ACL three times. Towards the end of his first full season with Minnesota, Shaw tore his ACL for a fourth time, putting his career in jeopardy. He dropped off the Wild’s depth chart and later joined the AHL’s Manitoba Moose for two seasons. Although he never returned to the NHL, Shaw’s two years in Manitoba went well. He finished his tenure having scored 32 goals and 81 points in 143 games with a -14 rating. Since returning to the Wild this past summer, Shaw has scored a team-leading three goals and nine points in nine games for Iowa. If he returns to the lineup throughout his call-up, Shaw will play his first NHL contest since April 15, 2024.

items.body: Register Login Jets Recall Elias Salomonsson By Brennan McClain | at October 24, 2026 6:00 pm As expected, the Winnipeg Jets have added a defenseman after Jack St. Ivany was claimed off waivers earlier today. According to a team announcement , the Jets recalled Elias Salomonsson from the AHL’s Manitoba Moose. Salomonsson, 22, has been ramping up in the AHL over the past week. He underwent the knife in April for shoulder surgery, and missed Winnipeg’s training camp and preseason while in recovery. Salomonsson has missed the Jets’ first ten games of the 2026-27 season, and it remains uncertain whether he will be in the lineup for the Heritage Classic tomorrow. Last season, the former second-round pick debuted for Winnipeg. He finished the 2025-26 season with one goal and five points in 32 games with a -6 rating, averaging 17:58 of ice time per game. Although his scoring output left something to be desired, his 51.8% CorsiFor and 91.2% on-ice SV% at even strength show uncommon maturity for a younger defenseman. Fortunately, Salomonsson should have another level to get to offensively. He’s shown it before in the AHL, scoring five goals and 27 points in 53 games throughout the 2024-25 campaign. During his pseudo-preseason over the past week, Salomonsson registered an assist in two games with a -1 rating. While Salomonsson replaced St. Ivany, the Jets will face a similar situation when Josh Morrissey returns from injured reserve due to an upper-body injury. Once Morrissey returns, Salomonsson will likely return to AHL Manitoba since he’s the only defenseman on the roster exempt from waivers.

items.body: SEATTLE — Relationships are complicated. Except for the relationship between Brady Tkachuk and the Ottawa Senators’ fan base, which was focused in sharp simplicity this week by the player’s return to bedlam — one smirking black hat wading into a sea of white ones. items.body: Register Login Could The Trade Market Favor The Buyers? By Josh Cybulski | at October 24, 2026 5:00 pm The NHL has seen a sellers’ market at the NHL Trade Deadline for at least the past few years, including this past year. The sellers’ market extended well into the draft and summer, as teams paid astronomical prices for top NHL-ready talent. The deadline is still over five months away, and there’s plenty of hockey to be played, but could this season have more sellers than in years past? Only time will tell, but given some teams’ slow starts, the NHL could see more sellers than in some years, which would be good news for buyers. Every year, some teams enter the deadline focused on the future, hoping to move pending unrestricted free agents and other veterans in exchange for future assets. Some teams that might otherwise be sellers instead try to remain competitive, even as their playoff chances fade. This season, with so many teams starting so poorly, it will be interesting to see whether some teams punt on their season earlier than in years past, hoping to beat the sellers’ market and move their assets before the market gets flooded with talent. Perhaps this is the thinking in Pittsburgh, where general manager Kyle Dubas and Penguins management are reportedly looking to move talent to make room for their young prospects. If the Penguins do become sellers, which is very possible given their struggles so far, they will have many chips to play. Defenseman Erik Karlsson is a pending UFA, as are superstar forwards Sidney Crosby and Evgeni Malkin . items.title: Ducks’ Leo Carlsson burns Flyers with goal and assist in win
items.summary: Leo Carlsson came within one financial decision of becoming a Philadelphia Flyer last summer. On Saturday, the Anaheim centre found a way to beat the team that tried to pry him away from the Ducks.
items.body: PHILADELPHIA — Leo Carlsson came within one financial decision of becoming a Philadelphia Flyer last summer. On Saturday, the Anaheim centre found a way to beat the team that tried to pry him away from the Ducks. Carlsson scored and assisted on the game-winner as the Ducks snapped a five-game losing streak with a 5-4 win over Philadelphia. “Attention was on some other guys, so I didn't really feel anything different about it, to be honest,” Carlsson said. “I was never really here, so it wasn't anything different.” The Flyers could use Carlsson's production. After his two-point game, he now leads the Ducks in scoring with 13 points (three goals, 10 assists). His goal was set up by Cutter Gauthier, the player he was referencing, who the fans were paying attention to, as their vitriolic chants still target Gauthier after forcing a trade from the Flyers in January 2024. The Flyers and Ducks have been linked multiple times in the past two years. After acquiring Jamie Drysdale for Gauthier, the Flyers also acquired Trevor Zegras from Anaheim. But the Flyers turned the NHL on it's ear when they tendered the 21-year-old Carlsson to a five-year, $90-million offer sheet on July 3. Its $18 million average annual value was the richest in NHL history at the time. Anaheim matched it six days later, a day before the deadline, keeping Carlsson through the 2030-31 season. Philadelphia kept the four first-round picks it would have owed as compensation. “Did we expect the offer sheet to be this high? No. We did not see that one coming,” Ducks general manager Pat Verbeek said at the time. “But we’re very confident, with the cap going up and the ability of Leo to make strides of improvement and become an elite player, we feel confident this contract will be a good one in the end.” Carlsson

However, that wasn’t enough to earn a roster spot at the end of training camp last month. Instead, he was assigned to the Firebirds, where he has been rather dominant early on. He has played in nine AHL contests so far, scoring nine goals while adding two assists. He has surpassed the 20-goal mark at that level in each of the last two years despite the amount of NHL time he has had. As for McCann, the team is still evaluating his injury so accordingly, there is no word yet on how long he might be out for. items.title: Quinn Hughes on Wild contract talks: ‘My two feet are planted in Minnesota’
items.summary: Quinn Hughes is enjoying his time with the Minnesota Wild, but the star defenceman stopped short of offering a definitive answer about his long-term future with the team.
items.body: Quinn Hughes is enjoying his time with the Minnesota Wild , but the star defenceman stopped short of offering a definitive answer about his long-term future with the team. "I'm where I've always been. I'm excited right now. My two feet are planted in Minnesota and, you know, something could happen soon. I'm not really too sure," Hughes told reporters Saturday , regarding contract talks. "I'm really enjoying playing here." The 27-year-old has quickly embraced his surroundings in Minnesota, highlighting the team's defensive group and the potential for further improvement when forward Brock Faber returns to the lineup. "... We have a great team," added Hughes. "First thing is, you want to get into the playoffs, but I would think that we have a chance to win this year." Hughes also said ahead of the season that he's plenty satisfied with the direction and state of the organization and simply hasn't thought much about the next phase of his career. “With planning out my future, I don’t do that. items.body: Register Login Blues Recall Quinton Burns By Brian La Rose | at October 24, 2026 2:44 pm With the Blues only carrying a minimum-sized roster at the moment, adding reinforcements at some point was a given. They’ve added one on the back end as they’ve recalled blueliner Quinton Burns from AHL Springfield, per the NHL’s media site. It’s the first career NHL recall for the 21-year-old. Burns was a third-round pick back in 2023 out of OHL Kingston, spending two more seasons with the Frontenacs after being selected. In 2024-25, he had a big season there, tallying 49 points and 100 penalty minutes in 66 contests. That production didn’t carry over to his first professional campaign last season. Burns split the year between the Thunderbirds and ECHL Florida. With the former, he had five assists and 92 penalty minutes in 31 games while with the latter, he collected six points and 17 penalty minutes in 16 appearances. This season, Burns has an assist and 29 penalty minutes through seven outings in Springfield. At first glance, it seems unlikely that Burns will see much action. Theo Lindstein , one of their top defensive prospects, could be back up before long after getting some game action in with the Thunderbirds; he made his season debut with them last night. For now, at least, Burns will get a chance to make an impression on the coaching staff in the hopes of making his NHL debut.

items.title: Sharks’ Adam Gaudette to make season debut against Bruins
items.summary: Gaudette missed the first four games of the season with an upper-body injury, and was a healthy scratch for the remaining seven.
items.body: Gaudette had initially missed game action due to an upper-body injury he had at the start of training camp. He did not play any preseason games, and began the regular season on non-roster injured reserve, but was activated after four games. He has since missed the previous seven games as a healthy scratch. Gaudette finally finds himself in the lineup as a result of an upper-body injury to winger Igor Chernyshov, who will be out on a week-to-week basis. With Chernyshov and Alexander Wennberg (also week-to-week with an upper-body injury) out, Gaudette was the only healthy forward on the Sharks roster, so he was their only option to enter the lineup. At this point in time, the Sharks haven’t made any corresponding roster moves in response to the injuries, whether that be placing Chernyshov and Wennberg on IR, or recalling a player from their AHL affiliate, the San Jose Barracuda. Gaudette is coming off of his best season in several years, where he had 17 goals and eight assists for 25 points in 66 games . It was his best scoring pace since his 2019-20 season, where he had 12 goals and 21 assists for 33 points in 59 games. After struggling to find an NHL role for most of his NHL career, Gaudette has established himself as a solid bottom-six scorer, good for 15-20 goals, in the past couple seasons. Gaudette will enter the lineup on the fourth line alongside Zack Ostapchuk and Barclay Goodrow. He has also appeared in 20 Stanley Cup Playoff games, where he’s recorded one goal and five assists for six points. McCann, a first-round pick for the Canucks in 2014, played three seasons of junior hockey in the Ontario Hockey League with the Soo Greyhounds. items.title: ‘I hope they know I care about them’: Hellebuyck sends positive message to Jets fans
items.summary: Star goalie Connor Hellebuyck addressed the media in New Jersey the day after he was traded from the Jets to the Devils.
items.body: Mehta had a lot to say about his process, philosophy on the goaltending position, and the work his front office did to facilitate the deal, but Hellebuyck struck a positive tone toward the fan base whose team he had just demanded out of after a 2025-26 season in which they missed the playoffs after claiming the Presidents’ Trophy the year prior. “There’s a lot that I need to say,” Hellebuyck said. “But they have the [Heritage Classic] coming up. So out of respect for them and the celebration of hockey, I’m going to postpone that to a later date. I hope they know I care about them.” Hellebuyck could have his first opportunity to play in front of the fans in Winnipeg when the Devils take on the Jets in Manitoba on November 10, but as Mehta shared during his availability, there has not been a plan put in place for Hellebuyck’s return to play. The 33-year-old has missed the entirety of training camp, the preseason and the regular season as he awaited a trade away from the Jets. The Michigan native leaves Winnipeg as the most decorated player in this iteration of Jets hockey. He captured three Vezina Trophies as the top goalie in the NHL, and in 2025, he became the first goalie to win the Hart Trophy since Carey Price a decade earlier. Hellebuyck backstopped Team USA to its first Olympic gold medal since 1980 last winter in Italy, putting together a performance for the ages in the gold medal game, an overtime win over Canada. Given those accolades, it’s no surprise that Hellebuyck was clearheaded about what’s on his mind now that he’s gotten the trade he wanted. “I’m here to win,” he said. “The only thing I’ve got left on my resume is a Stanley Cup. So seeing that these guys have kind of got their vision tight on that as well, it’s just going to fit perfectly.”

items.summary: The Ottawa Senators have placed winger Kurtis MacDermid on waivers.
items.body: Register Login Senators Place Kurtis MacDermid On Waivers By Brian La Rose | at October 24, 2026 1:07 pm The Senators are opening up a roster spot. Postmedia’s Bruce Garrioch reports ( Twitter link ) that winger Kurtis MacDermid has been placed on waivers. The veteran, who has also played defense at times in a pinch, was acquired in a swap of tough guys in the 2025 preseason, with Zack MacEwen going to New Jersey. However, the change of scenery didn’t result in a whole lot of playing time for the 32-year-old. He got into just 19 games, notching one assist, 33 penalty minutes, and 18 hits in just 4:12 per game of ice time. Unsurprisingly, he didn’t see any action in the playoffs. This season, MacDermid found himself with an injured/non-roster designation to start the season due to an upper-body injury. Today’s placement indicates that he has recovered from that injury since injured players can’t go through waivers. MacDermid has 307 career NHL appearances under his belt over parts of nine seasons between four different teams. His best showing offensively came back in 2019-20 with Los Angeles, when he had eight points in 45 games while he was taking a regular shift on the back end. In recent years, he has almost exclusively played on the fourth line as a pugilist. The veteran is in the final season of a three-year, one-way contract that carries a $1.15MM cap charge. If he passes through waivers unclaimed, Ottawa will still be able to clear the full amount off their books, nearly doubling their salary cap flexibility in the process. Teams will have until 1 PM CT on Sunday to decide if they want to add the gritty winger to the lineup. Otherwise, MacDermid will be heading for his first AHL stint since the 2018-19 campaign.

items.title: Breaking Down Connor Hellebuyck’s Discounted Cap Hit
items.summary: Breaking down the CBA rule that has yielded a discounted salary cap charge for the New Jersey Devils for Connor Hellebuyck this season.
items.body: Register Login Breaking Down Connor Hellebuyck’s Discounted Cap Hit By Brian La Rose | at October 24, 2026 12:30 pm The early assessment of Friday’s Connor Hellebuyck trade has drawn mixed reviews. Some think that the Devils acquired him at a discount while others think the Jets made out rather well. Regardless of your take on the matter, New Jersey did indeed acquire the veteran netminder at a discount. That is, a discount in his cap hit. Section 15.13 (a) of the CBA has a clause that says players who miss time in training camp without permission are subject to a fixed reduction in pay. The clause reads as follows: For each day a Player does not report during Training Camp without his Club’s permission, his pay shall be reduced by 1/275th of his annual Paragraph 1 NHL Salary specified in his SPC without limitation of any other contract rights it may have. Subsection (b) goes on to discuss the requirements for this rule to come into effect. Basically, Hellebuyck had to request an absence, the team had to respond no in writing and allow ample time for Hellebuyck to “cure” and recant his request. All of those things occurred, meaning the above rule was indeed applied. Hellebuyck’s regular cap hit is $8.5MM. Based on the 1/275th per day formula above, the reduced cap charge increases by $30,909.09 per day missed. Winnipeg’s training camp lasted 13 days and he obviously missed all of them. Thus, the reduction is 13 times the daily amount, or $401,818.20. That moves his cap charge from $8.5MM to $8,098,182. That will be Hellebuyck’s cap hit for the rest of the season, before reverting to the $8.5MM number starting in 2027-28 for the rest of his deal. items.title: Rangers Recall Matthew Robertson
items.summary: The New York Rangers have recalled defenseman Matthew Robertson from AHL Hartford.
items.body: Register Login Rangers Recall Matthew Robertson By Brian La Rose | at October 24, 2026 11:30 am After sending down Justin Dowling , the Rangers didn’t waste much time filling the vacated roster spot. The team announced ( Twitter link ) late Friday that defenseman Matthew Robertson has been recalled from AHL Hartford. With the recall, the team is now back to the maximum of 23 players on the active roster. The 25-year-old was basically a regular with New York last season, playing in 72 games. He chipped in offensively with six goals and a dozen assists in more than 17 minutes per game of playing time. Basically, it looked as if he had secured a spot on their full-time roster. Instead, the team reshaped their back end over the summer, bringing in Sean Durzi and Marcus Pettersson while fifth overall pick Alberts Smits has been an every-game regular. That pushed Robertson onto the waiver wire early this month, where he somewhat surprisingly passed through unclaimed. Robertson has suited up in six games for the Wolf Pack so far this season and has been fairly quiet offensively, collecting just one assist. He had surpassed the 20-point mark in each of his last three full seasons with them from 2022-23 through 2024-25. It’s unclear if Robertson’s promotion is to play him (perhaps to give Smits a night off) or hedging against injury with Durzi missing the last two practices. Either way, the Rangers need to get Robertson in at least six games with them this season to retain his RFA rights this summer. If they don’t, he’ll be eligible for Group Six unrestricted free agency in July.

items.title: Penguins place Sam Girard on injured reserve
items.summary: Girard last appeared in the Penguins’ lineup on Oct. 17 against the Golden Knights.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Pittsburgh Penguins will continue to be without one of their veteran defensemen for the time being, as the team announced on Saturday that it has placed Sam Girard on injured reserve. Girard has been out of the lineup since he suffered an injury during Pittsburgh’s loss to the Vegas Golden Knights on Oct. 17 when he was injured while trying to get back to make a play on defense. The veteran puck-mover is in his second year in the Steel City after coming over last season in a trade with the Colorado Avalanche , the team with which he had spent his entire career after the Avs chose him in the second round of the 2016 NHL Draft. Girard, who posted a career-high 37 points in 2022-23 in Denver, is off to a strong start offensively this year. Through just nine games, he’s already matched his post-trade output with the Pens last year in 20 games with seven points. Girard has skated to a minus-4 rating while playing an average of 18:44 of time on ice per game. For the entirety of his NHL career, Girard has racked up 38 goals and 211 assists for 249 points in 617 career games. In 2022, Girard had three points in seven games as he helped the Avalanche win the Stanley Cup. The Penguins, who are looking to replicate their effort from last season that saw them surprise the hockey world en route to a spot in the Stanley Cup Playoffs, are off to a rocky start to their 2026-27 campaign. After a 2-0-0 start, Pittsburgh dropped seven of its next eight games before waking up in a big way in a 4-0 victory over the Florida Panthers on Thursday. The Penguins host the Nashville Predators on Saturday night and will wrap up a three-game homestand against the Utah Mammoth next Thursday.

items.title: James Reimer becomes oldest goalie to record AHL shutout in nearly 20 years
items.summary: Reimer was signed by the New York Rangers’ AHL affiliate on a professional tryout last week.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: George Maddaloni/Hartford Wolf Pack A veteran netminder is making a little bit of history in the minors. On Friday night, the Hartford Wolf Pack, the American Hockey League affiliate of the New York Rangers , picked up a 2-0 win over the Boston Bruins’ top farm team, the Providence Bruins. In net for the Wolf Pack was James Reimer, who became the oldest goaltender to pitch a shutout in league history in almost two decades. At 38 years and 222 days old, Reimer became the eldest backstop to post a donut on the scoreboard since Wade Flaherty (40 years, 62 days old) posted a shutout while a member of the Rockford IceHogs on March 13, 2008. It was Reimer’s first AHL victory since Jan. 22, 2011, while he was with the Toronto Marlies, which just happened to be a shutout as well. Reimer now has five shutouts in his AHL career. It was Reimer’s first game of the season, as he had recently signed with the Wolf Pack on a professional tryout . The Winnipeg native came to the Rangers organization after the Blueshirts were hit with the injury bug in a big way, with Igor Shesterkin going down for the rest of the 2026-27 season and Joonas Korpisalo still being out of action. Reimer is trying to make another midseason comeback for the second year in a row. In 2025-26, he signed with the Ottawa Senators in January due to extended absences from Linus Ullmark and lackluster play from then-backup Leevi Merilainen. That came after he played one game for the Sens’ primary affiliate, the Belleville Senators, on a PTO. It’s not yet clear whether the Rangers will need to sign the 38-year-old, as Dylan Garand and Spencer Martin are holding down the fort in Manhattan.

That’s not an ideal track record, especially since Ristolainen is eligible to reach unrestricted free agency for the first time this summer. Signed at a $5.1MM cap charge, he’s impactful enough when healthy to command a raise while the Flyers have fielded trade inquiries for him for several years, though no offer has been good enough for them to pull the trigger on a swap. As for Wilson, his removal from the roster shouldn’t come as much of a surprise. He passed through waivers unclaimed on Friday, making him eligible to be sent down to the Phantoms. After consecutive losses in major international tournaments, an embarrassing showing at the 2025 Rivalry Series, and eight straight defeats at the hands of their hated rivals, something had to change. It started with management: head coach Troy Ryan and general manager Gina Kingsbury stepped down, leading to the hiring of Hockey Hall of Famer Daniele Sauvageau as GM. The Olympic gold medal-winning coach then promoted Kori Cheverie to head coach . With new voices in the front office, that has led to a sizeable shift in the group Hockey Canada will ice at the upcoming 2026 IIHF Women’s World Championship. The 25-player roster was released last week , and many of the big names are there – Sarah Fillier, Laura Stacey, Ann-Renee Desbiens, and Erin Ambrose, to name a few – but it’s the names that aren’t there, and the new ones that are, that are capturing the eyes of many around the game. Now, Marie-Philip Poulin’s absence was expected, as Captain Clutch is out for the foreseeable future after undergoing knee surgery over the summer. Mandatory Credit: James Guillory-Imagn Images We’ve reached a juncture of the NHL season in which it’s early and late. It’s early in the sense that the sample sizes are small, the calendar hasn’t yet reached November and every team has more than 70 games left on the schedule. It’s late in that some struggling outfits need to consider making drastic changes now while they can still save their seasons, and changing head coaches is usually the quickest fix to get results. So, Roundtable: Who will be the first NHL coach fired this season? MATT LARKIN: Does it count if the coach fires himself? There’s a non-zero chance Rick Bowness does that and walks away as Columbus Blue Jackets coach this season. He’s the oldest active bench boss in the league at 71, and he seems beyond fed up with his players’ compete level, regularly calling them out in post-game pressers going back to late last season. If he doesn’t decide he’s had enough, I wonder if GM Don Waddell makes the call and decides his players need a new voice. If it happens, it would mark the second consecutive year Columbus is the first team to fire its coach, as the axe fell on Dean Evason last January. items.body: NHL, NHLPA bring trophy to community ahead of Heritage Classic in Winnipeg PIKANGIKUM FIRST NATION, Ontario -- The teenager, clad in a black No. 63 Boston Bruins jersey, sat on the wooden stands in the Eenchokay Birchstick School gymnasium. He had visited the Stanley Cup moments earlier, but that could barely hold a candle to what came next for Neely Zdeno Turtle. That’s right, the boy wearing the Brad Marchand jersey was named after Cam Neely and Zdeno Chara , each a Bruins legend now in the Hockey Hall of Fame. The shy young man walked up to Andrew Ference , who was on hand as part of his role with the NHL’s Social Impact, Growth and Legislative Affairs department, to introduce himself to the member of the Bruins team that won the Cup in 2011. When Ference learned of Turtle’s homage to the Bruins greats, he reached Chara, the captain of the 2011 team, via a video call to excitedly tell him about this turn of events. The three chatted animatedly for a few minutes. “It’s absolutely unbelievable,” the 15-year-old said. “I didn’t expect him to call Chara. “It means a lot. Pikangikum is really remote, accessible only by plane and by winter (ice) road. This doesn’t happen every day and you have to take it all in. I watch a lot of hockey growing up and seeing that Cup in my face, it’s amazing. You see that Cup on TV and people hoisting it and now it’s right here.” Yes, the Stanley Cup was on this First Nations reserve -- a 4,470-acre plot of land on Pikangikum Lake that is a 45-minute flight from Winnipeg -- as part of a goodwill gesture by the NHL and the NHL Players’ Association. items.summary: All four of Montreal’s centres played reliable and predictable on Friday, which is exactly what the Canadiens will need to carry them through the adversity they’re facing without Nick Suzuki.
items.body: CHICAGO — It was on Friday afternoon that Montreal Canadiens coach Martin St. Louis said something specific to Oliver Kapanen that applied to all four of the centres he’d later depend on in a 4-1 win over the Chicago Blackhawks at United Center. “I think Oliver understands that hockey is not a one-on-one game,” St. Louis said. “It’s a team game; it’s a collective game with one-on-one moments. I don’t think Kappy’s a guy who’s searching for these one-on-one moments. I think he respects the rules of the game, the collective game on both sides of the puck, and I think that allows him to help the team on both sides and continue the actions, continue the offensive plays. He’s very predictable for his teammates… Wherever Kappy’s on the ice, and whether he’s going to touch it or whether he’s going to come back towards our zone, I know exactly what he’s going to do because he understands the rules.” So does Phillip Danault , who’s so far centred a line that, coming into Friday’s game, was tops in the NHL in expected-goals percentage among lines to have played at least 65 minutes together. items.title: Lightning captain Victor Hedman leaves game early
items.body: Tampa Bay Lightning captain Victor Hedman did not finish Friday's game. Hedman took only one shift in the second period and was not on the bench for the rest of the game as the Lightning lost 6-3 to the Colorado Avalanche. He finished the game with only 5:56 of ice time. The team did not announce a reason for his absence during the game and head coach Jon Cooper was not asked about Hedman's status post-game. Hedman, 35, had appeared in all 10 Lightning games so far this season, scoring two goals and four points. He missed the final month of the 2025-26 season due to what he later revealed was performance anxiety. "For me, it was not really feeling low, but it was performance anxiety, kind of feeling that pressure in your chest as soon as a game day would hit," Hedman said over the summer . "It kind of locks you up. You make a mistake and in the past you'd be able to shake it off, but I couldn't do that. And I wasn't feeling 100 per cent physically." Hedman is in his 18th NHL season. The Lightning continue their road trip at the Utah Mammoth on Saturday.

items.summary: Nathan MacKinnon had a goal and three assists, Nazem Kadri scored his first goal of the season and the Colorado Avalanche beat the Tampa Bay Lightning 6-3 on Friday night.
items.body: DENVER — Nathan MacKinnon had a goal and three assists, Nazem Kadri scored his first goal of the season and the Colorado Avalanche beat the Tampa Bay Lightning 6-3 on Friday night. Devon Toews, Fedor Svechkov, Artturi Lehkonen and Martin Necas also scored as Colorado rebounded from back-to-back road losses. Mackenzie Blackwood made 31 saves. Jake Guentzel scored twice and Charle-Edouard D’Astous added another for the Lightning, who saw their three-game winning streak halted. Nikita Kucherov was held in check and remains a goal or assist away from becoming the franchise's career points leader. He has 1,137 points and is tied with Steven Stamkos. Andrei Vasilevskiy stopped 18 of 23 shots, including one off the mask on MacKinnon's liner. Guentzel's goal with 42.7 seconds left in the second period made it 4-2. The Avalanche unsuccessfully challenged the play for a missed stoppage. The Lightning went on the power play but couldn't score. They struggled on the power play all evening. MacKinnon’s goal with 15:42 remaining gave Colorado a 5-2 cushion. Necas sealed it with a late empty-net tally. Logan O’Connor returned to the lineup after missing the start of the season with a lower-body injury. He recently lost his father, Myles, a former NHL defenseman, at age 59. The game featured the league's currently longest-tenured coaches in Jon Cooper and Jared Bednar. Cooper took over the Lightning in March 2013 and has won two Stanley Cups. Bednar was hired by Colorado in August 2016 and captured one Cup — in 2022 over the Lightning. Wyndham Clark, the 2026 U.S. Open champion, was in attendance and brought his trophy. Clark drank from the cup while receiving an ovation from the crowd.

items.title: Evans scores twice to lead Canadiens over Blackhawks
items.body: CHICAGO — Jake Evans scored twice and assisted on Kaiden Guhle’s goal and the Montreal Canadiens beat the Chicago Blackhawks 4-1 on Friday night. Evans’ third point, a feed to Guhle with 1:34 left in the second period, matched his career high. Montreal is 4-1-1 in its last six games, while Chicago has dropped two straight and four of its last six. A wide-open game tightened up late in the first period, which worked to Montreal’s advantage. Chicago opened the scoring on Connor Bedard ’s second goal of the season 4:23 in, but the Canadiens began to control the play, and by mid-period were limiting Chicago’s chances. Jacob Fowler, who made 20 saves, was lightly tested the rest of the game despite five Chicago power plays, and needed to make only three saves in the final period. Evans’ first goal of the game and season tied it with 2:31 left in the first. His second, a wrist shot over goalie Spencer Knight’s stick side with the Canadiens skating short-handed, gave Montreal a 2-1 lead 7:51 into the second period. Guhle also beat Knight on the stick side, his shot from the left point screened by Josh Anderson. Canadiens: At Winnipeg on Sunday for the outdoor Heritage Classic.

Unfortunately, Anaheim doesn’t have room for error with their defensive corps. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Edmonton Oilers announced Friday that goaltender Devon Levi has been placed on injured reserve. The team also announced they have recalled goaltender Matt Tomkins from their AHL affiliate, the Bakersfield Condors, under emergency conditions. Levi missed practice with the team on Friday, and according to Oilers Now reporter Bob Stauffer, Tristan Jarry will get the start Saturday against the Toronto Maple Leafs . Through seven games, Levi posted a 6-1-0 record with an .887 save percentage (SV%) and 3.11 goals against average (GAA). In 46 career NHL games, the native of Dollard-des-Ormeaux, Que., is 23-18-2 with an .893 SV% and 3.26 GAA with the Oilers and Buffalo Sabres . Levi, a seventh-round pick for the Florida Panthers in 2020, has appeared in 120 regular-season AHL games with the Rochester Americans across three seasons. He’s posted a 64-39-22 record with a .914 SV% and 2.52 GAA. He also played three seasons of college hockey with Northeastern University. In 66 career NCAA games, he went 38-22-6 with a .942 SV% and 1.90 GAA. As for Tomkins, the 32-year-old netminder has appeared in eight AHL seasons, where he’s posted a 59-57-19 record with a .903 SV% and 2.89 GAA. He’s also appeared in six career NHL games. The Oilers are 8-1-1 through their first 10 games of the 2026-27 regular season. They defeated the Carolina Hurricanes 6-5 in a shootout Thursday, thanks to a pair of five-point performances from captain Connor McDavid and forward Leon Draisaitl. They will host the Leafs Saturday. Puck drop is at 7 p.m. ET / 5 p.m. MT.

items.body: WINNIPEG — From an unheralded teenager playing in Odessa, Texas, plucked out of the fifth round, to becoming one of the premier goaltenders in the world. And what a circus it became over the last few months, as the Winnipeg Jets navigated the delicate nuances of trying to move a franchise cornerstone in a market plagued with contractual roadblocks, all while operating inside a goaltending market that almost always favours buyers. All of that finally came to a head on Friday, when the Jets traded Hellebuyck to the New Jersey Devils for a package that included immediate forward help, a couple of high-end prospects and some draft picks. "We took a chance on some gangly guy out of Odessa. But he's earned his way along the way. As an organization, we're proud of what we had accomplished; we wished we could have pushed it over the top." items.title: Mammoth sign Artem Duda to two-year contract extension
items.summary: The Utah Mammoth keep faith in Artem Duda’s rise with a new deal through the 2028-29 season.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Utah Mammoth has signed defenseman Artem Duda to a two-year contract extension, the hockey club announced Friday afternoon. The new deal will begin in the 2027-28 season and run through the end of 2028-29, with the first year as a two-way deal that will see him earn $900,000 in the NHL and $175,000 in the minors, with at least $220,000 guaranteed. In the second year of the contract, the deal becomes a one-way agreement, and he will be paid $950,000. Now 22 years old, Duda has played in parts of three American Hockey League seasons with the Tucson Roadrunners, scoring nine goals and 36 assists for 45 points over 103 regular-season games since entering the professional ranks. Initially selected in the second round of the 2022 NHL Draft by the Arizona Coyotes, Duda began his career in the CSKA Moskva development system and rose to play 14 KHL games in 2022-23, scoring three assists. After his brief KHL stint, the Coyotes looked to bring Duda to North America, but they couldn’t bring a Russian player into the CHL and couldn’t bring a teenager into the AHL. With limited options, the Coyotes worked out a deal with U Sports’ Toronto Metropolitan University, making Duda a rare NHL-drafted prospect to play in Canadian university hockey competitions. With the TMU Bold, he scored two goals and five assists in 12 games, helping the team advance to the national semifinal on home ice, before moving on to the AHL. Currently playing with Tucson, Duda has three points in six AHL games this season, with the Roadrunners sitting at 3-2-1, good for fifth in the AHL’s Pacific Division. He will look to make his NHL debut at some point in 2026-27, or in the next two years, as part of his newly signed deal.

items.body: Mercer, Daws among those going to Winnipeg for three-time Vezina winner, who asked to be dealt in offseason WINNIPEG -- Kevin Cheveldayoff said he can get some sleep again after the Winnipeg Jets general manager completed a trade that sent star goalie Connor Hellebuyck to the New Jersey Devils on Friday. “I’m very comfortable (with) what we accomplished here over the period of time,” Cheveldayoff said. “I certainly wish we could have done it four months ago, or whatever, when the opportunity started and we were looking (for a trade), but here we are here today.” Winnipeg acquired forwards Dawson Mercer and Nick Bjugstad , goalie Nico Daws , the rights to forward Alexander Command , a second-round pick in the 2029 NHL Draft and a seventh-round pick in the 2027 NHL Draft. That’s what I talked to Connor about today when I called him and wished him all the best. So, thank you very much to him and all his family.” The Jets suspended Hellebuyck on Sept. 16 for not reporting to training camp. The suspension was scheduled to end Friday. The trade came with the Jets getting ready to play the Montreal Canadiens outdoors in the 2026 Tim Hortons NHL Heritage Classic at Princess Auto Stadium here on Sunday (7 p.m. ET; TVAS, SN, TNT, truTV, HBO MAX). items.title: Official Opposition Leader Pierre Poilievre Latest To Tour Roustan Sports
items.summary: Today’s tour by the conservative leader followed visits from federal ministers Evan Solomon and Adam van Koeverden, making it three high-profile Canadian politicians on site at the Brantford, Ont., stick factory in less than two months.
items.body: Stephanie Bevan Stephanie Bevan Official Opposition Leader Pierre Poilievre Latest To Tour Roustan Sports Michael Traikos Partner Oct 23, 2026 9:39 PM Published Oct 23, 2026 9:39 PM Today’s tour by the conservative leader followed visits from federal ministers Evan Solomon and Adam van Koeverden, making it three high-profile Canadian politicians on site at the Brantford, Ont., stick factory in less than two months. Pierre Poilievre, the leader of the conservative party of Canada, visited Roustan Sports' stick factory on Friday, where he praised the Brantford, Ont., employees for carrying on a Canadian tradition in the midst of the U.S. trade war. Poilievre is the latest politician to visit the manufacturing facility, which is the sole wooden hockey stick manufacturing facility in Canada — and where 400,000 traditional wood sticks are manufactured yearly. Earlier this month, Adam van Koeverden , Canada’s Secretary of State (Sport), toured the Roustan Sports headquarters. Federal minister Evan Solomon visited in August. Poilievre was accompanied by Brantford mayor Kevin Davis, who will be running for the local Conservative Party of Canada seat in a yet-to-be-announced by-election. As Roustan Sports owner and CEO W. Graeme Roustan explained to media, Davis has been a supporter of the business since Roustan moved the factory from Hespeler, Ont. to Brantford in 2021. “All politicians in Canada recognize that hockey is not only our sport but the culture of our country," Roustan told the Brantford Expositor. “Having the only hockey stick factory in Canada creates a bit of a buzz. "They want to see this place, and walk the factory to see where hockey sticks are made. It’s really an experience.”

items.title: ‘Win today’: How Babcock’s honest, day-by-day approach has worked for Oilers
items.summary: Blunt. To the point. And when it comes to things hockey related, usually right. That’s what they told us we’d be getting when the Oilers brought in Mike Babcock, and so far, the advanced billing has been spot on.
items.body: EDMONTON — A month into the Mike Babcock era, we’re still waiting for a more telling exchange than the one our Elliotte Friedman had with Leon Draisaitl the day before training camp opened. Friedman: “What’s the most honest thing Mike Babcock has said to you so far?” We’ve all hated Draisaitl’s line changes here in Edmonton — but only for about 12 seasons and 856 career NHL games. Yet, it’s Babcock who watched some summer video and brought that back as his first take as Draisaitl’s new coach. Blunt. To the point. And when it comes to things hockey related, usually right. That is what they told us we’d be getting when the Oilers pulled Babcock out of coaching purgatory this summer, and so far, the advanced billing has been spot on. It’s become a funny place over the years, Edmonton, where the level of deference to the top players has existed on a sliding scale with how good those top players are. No one’s top players are as good as Edmonton’s, and as such, at times they were allowed at times to run amok. A decade without a Stanley Cup provided grounds for reflection, however, and so Connor McDavid , Draisaitl and Zach Hyman somewhat orchestrated the hiring of Babcock, pulling him out of enforced retirement for a job and a paycheck he certainly does not need. “You don't need it, so why do you do it? items.body: The Connor Hellebuyck trade caught the attention of many in the hockey world, with a host of opinions and reactions. items.body: Back in the summer of 2019, Tampa Bay netminder Andrei Vasilevskiy signed an eight-year contract with a $9.5 million cap hit. This was right after he won his first Vezina Trophy, but also right after his Presidents' Trophy-winning Lightning were swept out of the first round by Columbus. He was five years into his career at that point, but already established as one of the best in the game. Still, at the time, a $9.5 million cap hit for a goalie was a lot. Year 1 of his extension would count for 11.66 per cent of the cap, which today would be equivalent to about a $12.1 million AAV. No goalie makes that amount. Seven years later, Vasilevskiy's AAV is still second-highest among goalies, and he's since won two Stanley Cups and another Vezina. Why do we bring this up? Because at the time of Vasilevskiy's signing, our Cap Comparables article analyzing the deal explored the pros and cons of spending so much money on a position with two juxtaposing realities: a) it's the most important position to the success of your hockey club and b) it's the most difficult one to get right. The graveyard of flash-in-the-pan goalies is large, while those worth such a salary are few and far between. We compared the value of NHL goalies to that of an NFL running back. The idea that "running backs don't matter" in football came from evidence that it may not be prudent to pay a premium for the position when the offensive line blocking for them is so important to any runner's success. items.body: Register Login Wild Place Daemon Hunt On Waivers By Brennan McClain | at October 23, 2026 2:53 pm As the Minnesota Wild continue to reintroduce injured players to the lineup, other players will suffer the consequences. Today, that player is defenseman Daemon Hunt , whom the Wild announced they have placed on waivers. Presumably, Minnesota will assign Hunt to the AHL’s Iowa Wild if he clears. Given that he is strictly a depth defenseman, even at his age, the Wild shouldn’t have any issues passing him through the wire. In the NHL, Hunt has only played for Minnesota. The Wild selected him with the 65th overall pick in the 2020 NHL Draft. Since becoming a full-time professional player for the 2022-23 season, most of Hunt’s professional career has been spent in the Wild organization. Early into the 2024-25 season, Minnesota traded Hunt to the Columbus Blue Jackets as part of the package for David Jiříček . During his tenure with the Blue Jackets organization, he played only for the AHL’s Cleveland Monsters, scoring two goals and 14 points in 48 games with a -8 rating. He re-signed with Columbus the following offseason, but the Wild claimed him off waivers before the regular season. In a similar role, Hunt spent the entire 2025-26 season with Minnesota. He finished the campaign with six assists in 32 games with a -3 rating, averaging 12:26 of ice time per game. This year, Hunt has been held scoreless in 11 contests, while averaging 14:08 of ice time per night. If he is assigned to AHL Iowa after clearing waivers, it’ll be his first AHL appearance since the 2024-25 season.

items.title: Grading the Hellebuyck trade: Devils (finally) get their goalie as Jets head for uncertain future
items.summary: As Winnipeg laments the loss of a franchise legend, Jersey GM Mehta looks like a genius.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Rob Gray-Imagn Images The Connor Hellebuyck era is over in Winnipeg . The signature player of the Jets’ second iteration, Hellebuyck won everything but the Stanley Cup in Manitoba, collecting three Vezina Trophies and a Hart Trophy. Hellebuyck had grown vocally discontent with Winnipeg’s lackluster follow-up to a Presidents’ Trophy win in 2024-25, though, having apparently lost confidence that the Jets in front of him could compete as he waded into his late prime. Suspended without pay for skipping camp, ‘Bucky’ crossed the Rubicon and forced an exit from the only organization he’s ever known. An acrimonious end to a brilliant tenure in the prairies opened the door for the New Jersey Devils and GM Sunny Mehta, who had kept his interest in a player his predecessor, Tom Fitzgerald, had long courted close to the vest. The Devils have been searching for a goalie since Corey Schneider’s prime, which, as you may know, was a while ago. They have one now in Hellebuyck, who would walk into the Hall of Fame on his first try if he retired today. Will he do what Jacob Markstrom could not and complete Jersey’s Cup-contention puzzle? The Jets, meanwhile, have needed an out from their reliance on Hellebuyck and a thirtysomething core for some time. That one seed back in 2025 felt like this roster’s last real chance at the Cup during its collective prime, and a scorched-earth rebuild was never on the cards given how closely Winnipeg’s survival as a franchise is tied to its season-ticket sales. That means getting value via trades in lean years, especially for players of Hellebuyck’s quality. Can Dawson Mercer, young Alexander Command, and Co. help the Jets delay their decline? items.body: On a day dominated by Connor Hellebuyck, the Winnipeg Jets have been making other moves behind the scenes. Vlad Namestnikov has been placed on injured reserve retroactively following an injury picked up on October 15. The forward started the season with just one assist through six games for a lacklustre Jets team that sits 4-3-3. Other roster moves had to be made to make space for players coming in from the Hellebuyck trade, with Brayden Yager loaned to the Manitoba Moose and Jack St. Ivany placed on waivers, also for a loan to the Moose. Both players have featured on four occasions for the Jets this year, with neither registering a point. Winnipeg continues their season at home against the Montreal Canadiens on Sunday (7 p.m. ET / 4 p.m. PT on Sportsnet and Sportsnet+), looking to snap a four-game losing streak.

items.summary: Defensemen Daemon Hunt and Jack St. Ivany are available to be claimed.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Matt Blewett-Imagn Images A couple of NHL blueliners have just become available. On Friday, the Minnesota Wild placed defenseman Daemon Hunt on waivers, while the Winnipeg Jets placed defenseman Jack St. Ivany on waivers. Both players are now available to be claimed by any of the other 31 NHL teams. If they clear waivers, they’ll be eligible to be assigned to the American Hockey League (AHL). In 32 games for Minnesota last season, the Brandon, Manitoba native had no goals and six assists while averaging about 12 and a half minutes of ice time. He also contributed no goals and an assist over five playoff games for the Wild. The 6’1″, left-shot defenseman was selected by Minnesota in the third round of the 2020 NHL Entry Draft. He is known as a solid skater with good puck-moving ability. St. Ivany, 27, has no points in four games played with the Jets this season, while averaging about 13 and a half minutes of ice time. Winnipeg acquired St. Ivany from the Pittsburgh Penguins this past offseason in exchange for forward David Gustafsson. The Manhatten Beach, California native played 20 games for Pittsburgh last season, registering no goals and seven assists while averaging about 16 and a half minutes of ice time. items.title: Oilers’ Mattias Ekholm out vs. Maple Leafs with concussion
items.body: The Edmonton Oilers will be without one of their top defenceman on Saturday. Mattias Ekholm will be sidelined against the Toronto Maple Leafs (7 p.m. ET / 4 p.m. PT on Sportsnet and Sportsnet+) with a concussion, head coach Mike Babcock told reporters on Friday. Ekholm suffered the concussion in a collision with Carolina's William Carrier in the third period of the Oilers' win over the Hurricanes on Thursday. He appeared to hit his head on the ice as he attempted to play the puck in his own zone before the hit from Carrier. He stayed on his knees as he was attended to by the trainers. Ekholm eventually got to his feet and made his way off the ice, but appeared unsteady and needed assistance from teammates.

items.body: Forward still has fond feelings for former teammates after trade to Washington ARLINGTON, Va. -- Alex Tuch anticipates facing his former Buffalo Sabres teammates when they visit the Washington Capitals at Capital One Arena on Saturday (7 p.m. ET; MNMT, MSG-B) will be “a little bit different.” It’s also an experience the 30-year-old forward is looking forward to, though. “I’ve just got a big, dumb smile on my face just thinking about playing against those guys and loving them to death and miss them,” Tuch said Friday. “But really happy where I am right now and it's going to be a really hard-fought battle.” Tuch played five seasons for the Sabres, the team he grew up rooting for in Syracuse, New York, and and helped them end their 14-season Stanley Cup Playoff drought last season before their Cup dreams ended with 3-2 overtime loss to the Montreal Canadiens in Game 7 of the Eastern Conference Second Round. He was unable to agree with Buffalo on a new contract after last season, so instead of losing Tuch as an unrestricted free agent, the Sabres worked out a sign-and-trade deal with the Capitals that was completed on June 24 after he signed an eight-year, $84 million contract. Buffalo received a third-round pick in the 2027 NHL Draft and the rights to forward David Kampf , an unrestricted free agent who was not re-signed. Tuch, a three-time 30-goal scorer who was second on Buffalo in goals (33) and third in points (66) in 79 games last season, has provided everything Washington (5-4-0) hoped he would. Asked to shift from his natural right wing to the left side to fill a team need, he leads the Capitals in goals (five), is second in points (seven), plays in all situations and ranks first among their forwards in averaging 18:48 in ice time through nine games. Toronto Maple Leafs forward Gavin McKenna , the No. 1 pick at the 2026 NHL Draft, says it defies logic. “I think now having a taste of what the NHL is like, it just makes it that much crazier,” McKenna said Friday. “It's like every night you just are expecting him to put up five points. I don't know how he's doing it. I got to skate with him this summer, and kind of see what he was like, and it's, he's out of this world.” Others, like Maple Leafs forward Jack Roslovic , a teammate of McDavid last season, can only shake their head and laugh. “I was living it, I saw it every night,” Roslovic said. “When you get a player like that, he's just going to eat for the majority of the time, just because of who he is, and if I were a coach, I'd probably do the same thing (and keep running him out).” It’s safe to say McDavid’s historic start has not gone unnoticed by the Maple Leafs ahead of their first meeting against the Oilers this season Saturday at Rogers Place in Edmonton (7 p.m. ET; SNO, SNW, SNP). As part of his 10-game point streak to start the season, McDavid had at least five points in a game three times. The third time came Thursday, when he had two goals and three assists in a 6-5 shootout win against the Carolina Hurricanes. items.summary: Pushing not quite all-in to acquire Connor Hellebuyck instantly elevates the New Jersey Devils, hurts their divisional opponents, and creates a new perception around the team. As for the Winnipeg Jets? Well, the less said, the better.

As for the Winnipeg Jets? Well, the less said, the better. It turns out that Sunny Mehta was playing some four-dimensional chess. Back in September, he told NHL.com , "Goaltending has changed dramatically during the past 20 years... items.title: Sunny Mehta bluffed the hockey world on goaltending
items.summary: Over the summer, the new Devils GM described himself as “reluctant to invest significant assets” in the goalie position.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources The New Jersey Devils stunned the hockey world on Friday when they landed disgruntled superstar goalie Connor Hellebuyck in a blockbuster trade with the Winnipeg Jets . While the top contenders for Hellebuyck were reportedly the Buffalo Sabres , Utah Mammoth and Carolina Hurricanes , the Devils swooped in with an offer built around prospect Alexander Command and 24-year-old forward Dawson Mercer to obtain the three-time Vezina Trophy-winning goalie. The surprise is only augmented by Devils general manager Sunny Mehta’s comments about the goalie position he made after taking over in the role this summer. Mehta publicly downplayed the notion that he would spend big on a goalie, telling NHL.com in an interview that he was “reluctant to invest significant assets” in the position. items.title: Whitecloud committed to future with Flames: ‘Calgary is home’
items.summary: While the Flames continue to navigate a rebuild that has left fans wondering who might be the next veteran out the door, Zach Whitecloud insists he wants to be part of the solution.
items.body: CALGARY — Zach Whitecloud has designs on spending Christmas Day at an outdoor rink near his Altadore home, sticks in the middle, with a handful of friends, neighbours and family members skating around in the snow. It’s a wonderful image for a guy who spent much of his career in places where outdoor hockey was more of a novelty than a neighbourhood tradition. It’s also a pretty good indication of where the Calgary Flames defenceman sees his future. And while the Flames continue to navigate a rebuild that has left fans wondering who might be the next veteran out the door, Whitecloud insists he’s a guy who would rather help build something than seek greener/warmer pastures. At this rate, the Oilers captain will secure his 10th career 100-point season two and a half weeks before Christmas and break Wayne Gretzky’s single-season record by a mere 45 points. But the Oilers’ stylistic transformation under new coach Mike Babcock has also played a part in the team’s 8-1-1 start. Specifically, Edmonton has ditched the run-and-gun approach and started dumping in pucks at a much higher clip, which in turn has improved its defensive play. “We want to limit turnovers, obviously,” McDavid told reporters earlier this week. “We’re talking about playing better defence, and part of that is being responsible with the puck and managing the puck. I think you’re seeing that throughout the lineup, understanding when’s the time to attack and when’s the time to get on the forecheck. We want to be a heavy team. We want to forecheck pucks back. (We’ve) done that at times. We’ve gotten away from it at times, and we don’t have success. We’re trying to find the right formula.” Across the Oilers’ first two seasons under previous coach Kris Knoblauch, they were one of the NHL’s top defensive teams, finishing sixth and fifth, respectively, in expected goals against per game en route to back-to-back Stanley Cup Final appearances. Those defensive details slipped last season, however, as the Oilers fell to 19th in that category. Combined with goaltending that ranked 28th in total goals saved above expected, that ultimately cost the Oilers, who lost in the first round of the playoffs. items.title: Oilers’ dynamic duo dominated against reigning Cup champs
items.summary: McDavid and Draisaitl had a combined 10 points in the Oilers’ 6-5 shootout win over the Hurricanes Thursday.
items.body: The dynamic duo had a combined 10 points in the Oilers’ 6-5 shootout win over the Carolina Hurricanes Thursday night, a game that saw the two former Hart Trophy winners go toe-to-toe with the defending Stanley Cup champions. The game also saw history be made, as McDavid became the fourth player in NHL history to record at least 30 points through the first 10 games of a season. On Friday’s episode of Daily Faceoff LIVE , Tyler Yaremchuk is joined by The Sheet host Jeff Marek to discuss the Oilers’ win over the Hurricanes and how dominant the combination of McDavid and Draisaitl are in Edmonton. Tyler Yaremchuk : That was one of the better October hockey games that we’ve seen in recent memory. No matter which way you dice it: with Connor McDavid, the start to the season he’s had, is having absolutely jaw-dropping. This does not happen very often: he has broken a Wayne Gretzky record. That just doesn’t happen. McDavid broke the Oilers’ franchise record for most points in the first 10 games of a season with his 31st point Thursday night. He went into a game against the best team in the Eastern Conference, and I was sitting there going, “Hey, this is going to be a quieter night, Carolina is known for playing that tight defensive system … it was fun for McDavid to average 2.8 points per game while it lasted.” Then what does he do? He puts up five points, and the duo of him and Leon Draisaitl combine for 10 points. They were in on every single one of Edmonton’s five goals, including a tying goal with less than 90 seconds to go to send the game into overtime. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Steven Ellis The Connor Hellebuyck saga has finally come to an end. The Winnipeg Jets shipped the star goaltender to the New Jersey Devils on Friday afternoon, giving the Devils one of the best netminders in the world. So, what are the Jets getting in forward Alexander Command, the prospect included in the deal? Command entered the 2026 NHL Draft as one of the safest center options available. A tag like that can sound concerning to some fans, as “safe” picks often lack high-end upside. But many scouting departments see things differently. They prioritize reliable players with a clear developmental trajectory toward the NHL, and Command checked almost every box. The Devils liked what they saw, selecting him 12th overall back in June, and was later listed as the team’s third top prospect by DFO. Command’s draft season was an impressive one. He posted 17 goals and 44 points with Örebro’s U-20 program. He also racked up seven points at the U-18 World Championship, helping Sweden capture gold while playing some of the best two-way hockey of anyone in the tournament. Command failed to register a point in six SHL appearances last year, but he logged only about 11 total minutes of ice time across those outings. He surpassed that total in his first SHL game back in October, but his ice time dwindled with every passing game, and he remains scoreless through another six appearances at Sweden’s top level. items.body: Defenseman who 'signed here for a reason' concerned with wins, not outside noise NEWARK, N.J. -- Dougie Hamilton doesn't view his 15th NHL season as an audition or an opportunity to answer those who wondered whether his time with the New Jersey Devils was ending. After more than 900 NHL games, a few injuries, and a season in which his name circulated in trade speculation, the 33-year-old defenseman understands some judgments are out of his control. "I don't think so," Hamilton told NHL.com when asked if he entered this season feeling he had something to prove. "There's lots of different things going on, and I think for me, it's proving to yourself and doing your best. "At the end of the day, you've got to look yourself in the mirror every day. If you're putting as much work as you can and doing your best, then that's all you can do." Those familiar with Hamilton know that's a typical response, always understated but certain. He signed with New Jersey for a reason, a seven-year, $63 million contract on July 28, 2021, carrying an average annual value of $9 million through the 2027-28 season. "I mean, this is where I am; I signed here," Hamilton said. "I like being here, and I signed here for a reason. … You want to be somewhere that you're wanted and feel valued." Hamilton's name surfaced in trade rumors last season after injuries limited him to 84 games over two seasons, including a torn pectoral muscle that required surgery in 2023-24 and another injury absence in 2024-25. This season, he's looked like the player the Devils envisioned when they made him one of the NHL's highest-paid defensemen in 2021. items.title: Jets deal Connor Hellebuyck to Devils, ending trade-request saga
items.body: The Winnipeg Jets traded the three-time Vezina Trophy winner to the New Jersey Devils for prospect Alexander Command, goalie Nico Daws , forwards Dawson Mercer and Nick Bjugstad , a 2029 second-round pick and a 2027 seventh-round pick, the teams announced on Friday. Hellebuyck's move to New Jersey ends a saga that dates back to the goalie's trade request after last season. The veteran netminder confirmed the request in August, then did not show up to training camp, prompting an unpaid suspension from the team that was set to end Friday, two days before Winnipeg hosts the Heritage Classic against the Montreal Canadiens. Instead, Hellebuyck will head to a Devils team that sits 6-4-0 through 10 games this season. The prize of Winnipeg's return may be Command, the Swedish forward who was selected 12th overall by New Jersey at the draft in June. The 18-year-old is off to a fast start in the junior Swedish Hockey League this season, posting seven goals and five assists in six games for Orebro HK Jr., though he's been held off the scoresheet in six games at the senior level. Mercer, 24, has scored between 17 and 27 goals in each of his first five seasons, playing all 82 games in each instance. He has not scored yet this season, though he does have four assists. Daws, 25, has appeared in 59 NHL games (including four this year) with a career .897 save percentage and 2.94 goals-against average. The native of Munich, Germany, was New Jersey’s third-round pick (84th overall) in 2020 and has a 26-26-1 record with a shutout. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: David Kirouac-Imagn Images The Toronto Maple Leafs have taken another loss on their blueline. In corresponding moves, the Leafs have called up defensemen Dakota Mermis and Cole McWard from their American Hockey League (AHL) affiliate Toronto Marlies. The injury occured when he was checked hard into the boards by Rangers forward Will Cuylle in the third period, forcing him to miss the remainder of the game. The Washington, Michigan native has a goal and an assist for two points in six games this season, averaging just over 13 minutes of ice time. He attended Toronto’s training camp this year on a professional tryout agreement and ultimately secured a one-year, $1.4 million contract . Blankenburg split last season between the Nashville Predators and Colorado Avalanche , notching eight goals and 16 assists for 24 points over a total of 61 games. He is now in his sixth NHL season after signing with the Columbus Blue Jackets as an undrafted free agent in 2022. Rifai, 28, will be out week-to-week with a lower-body injury.
